newsitem.title: USA: Medicare, tax details seen key to U.S. budget pact.
newsitem.headline: Medicare, tax details seen key to U.S. budget pact.

text.p: The Clinton administration and Republicans were close to an agreement to balance the budget by 2002 but Medicare cost reduction and details of tax cuts were still an obstacle, a key Democrat said on Thursday.

"The big parameters are about to be settled I think. The devil however still is in the details and that's particularly true of tax cuts," said John Spratt of South Carolina, ranking democrat on the House Budget Committee.

"The White House and the Republican leadership were negotiating to late last night trying to reach final agreement and there's still some disagreement on the net amount of Medicare cost reduction and on the net tax cuts but they're within striking distance," Spratt told CNN television news.
Spratt said the net tax cut would be around $80 billion to $90 billion over five years as the agreement now stood, including a capital gains tax cut, estate tax relief and a child tax credit.
He said Democrats in particular wanted to see details on a capital gains tax cut and estate tax relief, not just a broad number but some content.
Budget talks were to continue Thursday. President Bill Clinton has said he hoped to conclude an agreement prior to his departure on Monday for Mexico.
